I am 72 years old and have farmed this land all my life. My family depends on this quarter-hectare plot of beans and cowpea, which we intercrop with sorghum to make the most of our sandy soil. I will apply one bag of the government-subsidized NPK fertilizer per hectare and spread cow manure to help the soil, because the land here in the North West is tired. I must also spray pesticide for the pod-borer insects that ruin cowpea every year, but we will use our own saved seeds and rely on my children and grandchildren for the labor since we have no money to hire workers, and rain is our only water.
